title: The Growing Danger of Fake AI Doctors on Social Media
subtitle: New research shows that AI-generated experts are spreading false health advice, causing concern among medical professionals.

summary.en: Recent research reveals a surge in AI-generated doctors on social media platforms like TikTok. These fake experts are spreading dangerous health myths to millions of viewers. Medical leaders warn that this misinformation is a serious threat to public health. Experts are calling on social media companies to take stronger action against this content. Patients are encouraged to be more careful about where they get their medical information.
summary.zh: 近期研究揭露，在 TikTok 等社群媒體平台上，人工智慧生成的假醫師數量激增。這些假專家正向數百萬名觀眾散布危險的健康迷思。醫療界領袖警告，這些錯誤資訊對公共衛生構成嚴重威脅。專家呼籲社群媒體公司針對此類內容採取更強硬的行動，並鼓勵病患在獲取醫療資訊時應更加謹慎。

paragraphs.en: The rise of artificial intelligence has brought many new tools to our daily lives, but it has also created a dangerous new trend: the fake AI-generated doctor. Following our previous reports on this issue, new research from the digital marketing agency Hallam has highlighted just how common these false experts have become. These accounts, which use AI to create realistic-looking avatars that resemble real doctors, are now reaching millions of people on social media platforms like TikTok.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智慧的興起為我們的日常生活帶來了許多新工具，但也創造了一種危險的新趨勢：人工智慧生成的假醫師。繼我們之前對此議題的報導後，數位行銷代理商哈勒姆 (Hallam) 的最新研究凸顯了這些假專家已變得多麼普遍。這些帳號利用人工智慧製作出外觀逼真的虛擬替身，看起來就像真正的醫師，目前在 TikTok 等社群媒體平台上已觸及數百萬人。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the scale of this problem is significant. In their study of top health-related videos, researchers found that 40% of the content was created or assisted by AI. When users searched for simple terms like “health tips,” that number jumped to 84%. These videos are not just harmless entertainment; they are spreading false information that could have serious consequences for public safety. Some of these AI doctors have shared disproven myths, such as the false claim that using deodorants or keeping a phone near your bed while sleeping can cause cancer. These claims have been clearly refuted by organizations like Cancer Research UK.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》(The Guardian) 報導，這個問題的規模相當驚人。在針對熱門健康相關影片的研究中，研究人員發現 40% 的內容是由人工智慧創作或輔助生成的。當使用者搜尋「健康小撇步」等簡單詞彙時，這個數字更飆升至 84%。這些影片不僅僅是無害的娛樂，它們正在散布可能對公共安全造成嚴重後果的錯誤資訊。其中一些人工智慧醫師分享了已被證偽的迷思，例如錯誤宣稱使用止汗劑或睡覺時將手機放在床邊會導致癌症。這些說法已被英國癌症研究協會 (Cancer Research UK) 等組織明確駁斥。

paragraphs.en: Beyond simple myths, these AI accounts are also promoting strange and potentially harmful remedies. One example discovered by researchers involved a fake product called “Hyalethinap Plus Pro Max.” An AI avatar claimed this product could fix everything from hair loss to joint pain. However, investigators could not find any evidence that this product actually exists. Other videos suggested using mixtures like Coca-Cola and onion as a pain-relief remedy. Experts warn that these videos are designed to get “clicks” and attention rather than provide real medical help.
paragraphs.zh: 除了簡單的迷思外，這些人工智慧帳號還在推廣奇怪且可能有害的療法。研究人員發現的一個例子涉及一種名為「Hyalethinap Plus Pro Max」的虛擬產品。一個人工智慧虛擬替身聲稱該產品可以解決從掉髮到關節疼痛的所有問題。然而，調查人員找不到任何證據證明該產品確實存在。其他影片則建議使用可樂和洋蔥的混合物作為止痛偏方。專家警告，這些影片的設計目的是為了獲取「點擊率」和關注，而非提供真正的醫療協助。

paragraphs.en: Medical professionals are deeply worried about the impact this is having on patients. Dr. Emma Runswick, deputy chair of the British Medical Association, warned that these AI accounts are peddling medical myths and fake miracle cures. She stated that platforms like TikTok must do more to stop the spread of this dangerous advice, or the public will pay the price with their health. Prof. Frankie Swords, the national medical director at NHS England, echoed these concerns. She noted that many doctors are seeing more patients who feel worried or confused because they have seen false advice online.
paragraphs.zh: 醫療專業人員對此現象對病患造成的影響深感擔憂。英國醫學會 (British Medical Association) 副主席艾瑪·朗斯威克 (Emma Runswick) 醫師警告，這些人工智慧帳號正在兜售醫療迷思和虛假的奇蹟療法。她表示，像 TikTok 這樣的平台必須採取更多行動來阻止這些危險建議的傳播，否則大眾將付出健康作為代價。英格蘭國民保健署 (NHS England) 的國家醫療主任法蘭琪·史沃茲 (Frankie Swords) 教授也呼應了這些擔憂。她指出，許多醫師發現越來越多病患因為在網路上看到錯誤建議而感到擔憂或困惑。

paragraphs.en: This trend is particularly worrying because of how many people now turn to social media for health guidance. A poll conducted by Savanta for the group Healthwatch England found that about one in five people use social media as a source for health information. William Pett, an official at Healthwatch England, explained that many people lack the skills to tell the difference between reliable medical advice and commercial hype. This makes it very easy for users to be misled by content that looks professional but is actually created by a computer program.
paragraphs.zh: 這種趨勢之所以特別令人擔憂，是因為現在有許多人轉向社群媒體尋求健康指引。由薩凡塔 (Savanta) 為英國健康觀察組織 (Healthwatch England) 進行的一項民調發現，約有五分之一的人將社群媒體作為健康資訊來源。英國健康觀察組織的官員威廉·佩特 (William Pett) 解釋說，許多人缺乏分辨可靠醫療建議與商業炒作的能力。這使得使用者很容易被那些看起來專業，但實際上是由電腦程式生成的內容所誤導。

paragraphs.en: Alex Ruani, a researcher at UCL who studies health misinformation, described the situation as an “industrialised exploitation of trust.” Because these avatars look and sound like real doctors, viewers are naturally more likely to believe what they say. This creates a high level of risk for anyone looking for genuine medical help. While TikTok has taken down some of the specific examples shared by researchers, the sheer volume of AI-generated content makes it difficult to control.
paragraphs.zh: 倫敦大學學院 (UCL) 研究健康錯誤資訊的研究員亞歷克斯·魯阿尼 (Alex Ruani) 將這種情況描述為「對信任的工業化剝削」。由於這些虛擬替身看起來和聽起來都像真正的醫師，觀眾自然更容易相信他們所說的話。這對於任何尋求真正醫療協助的人來說，都造成了極高的風險。雖然 TikTok 已經下架了研究人員分享的部分特定案例，但人工智慧生成內容的龐大數量使得監管變得困難。

paragraphs.en: As this technology continues to improve, the challenge of identifying fake medical advice will likely grow. The consensus among health experts is clear: social media platforms must take greater responsibility for the content they host. Until then, the public is urged to be extremely cautious. If you are looking for medical advice, it is always safer to speak with a real, qualified doctor rather than trusting an avatar on your screen. The health of the public depends on the ability to find information that is based on science, not on computer-generated lies.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著這項技術持續進步，辨識假醫療建議的挑戰可能會日益增加。健康專家們的共識很明確：社群媒體平台必須對其託管的內容承擔更大的責任。在此之前，大眾被敦促務必極度謹慎。如果您正在尋求醫療建議，與真正的合格醫師交談永遠比信任螢幕上的虛擬替身來得安全。大眾的健康取決於我們是否有能力找到基於科學，而非電腦生成的謊言之資訊。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To sell or promote ideas or goods, often those that are false or unwanted.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 兜售、散布（通常指不實或不好的觀念或商品）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞或指販賣實體物品，這裡指散布錯誤資訊。文中：Dr. Emma Runswick, deputy chair of the British Medical Association, warned that these AI accounts are peddling medical myths and fake miracle cures.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To repeat or support an opinion or idea that someone else has already expressed.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（回音），這裡指贊同並重複他人的看法。文中：Prof. Frankie Swords, the national medical director at NHS England, echoed these concerns.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Exaggerated publicity or promotion intended to make people excited about something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在商業語境中指為了吸引注意而進行的過度宣傳。文中：William Pett, an official at Healthwatch England, explained that many people lack the skills to tell the difference between reliable medical advice and commercial hype.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To remove something from the internet or a public place.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「寫下」或「拆除」，這裡指將網路上的內容刪除。文中：While TikTok has taken down some of the specific examples shared by researchers, the sheer volume of AI-generated content makes it difficult to control.

previousArticles.title: The Rise of Fake AI Doctors: A Growing Danger to Public Health
previousArticles.summaryEn: New research shows that AI-generated doctors are becoming common on social media platforms like TikTok. These fake experts often share false health advice, such as dangerous myths about cancer. Medical professionals are concerned because these videos can confuse patients and lead them to try harmful remedies. Experts are calling for social media companies to take stronger action to stop the spread of this misinformation. It is becoming harder for the public to tell the difference between real medical advice and fake content.

quiz.question: According to the research cited by The Guardian, how does the prevalence of AI-assisted content change when users search for 'health tips'?

options.A: It remains consistent at 40% of all health-related videos.
options.B: It increases significantly to 84% of the content.
options.C: It becomes the primary source of information for 20% of users.
options.D: It decreases because users are more likely to find official NHS content.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，研究指出在一般的健康相關影片中，AI 內容佔 40%；但當搜尋關鍵字為「health tips」時，比例大幅跳升至 84%。選項 A 混淆了整體比例與特定搜尋比例；選項 C 提到的 20% 是來自第五段關於使用社群媒體作為資訊來源的人口比例，而非影片內容比例；選項 D 在文中並未提及。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the motivations behind the creation of AI medical avatars?

options.A: They are created by medical professionals to reach a wider audience.
options.B: They aim to provide affordable healthcare to those who cannot see a doctor.
options.C: They are primarily driven by the desire for engagement and financial gain.
options.D: They are designed to test the public's ability to distinguish between science and fiction.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第三段，專家指出這些影片的設計目的是為了獲得「點擊率」(clicks) 和關注，而非提供真正的醫療協助。文中也提到這些產品通常不存在，暗示其商業炒作性質。選項 A 與文意相反，醫生們對此深感擔憂；選項 B 無法由文中推論，因為這些建議通常是錯誤且有害的；選項 D 並非創作者的目的，這只是研究者觀察到的社會現象。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does the phrase 'industrialised exploitation of trust' imply about the use of AI avatars?

options.A: The avatars are being used to mass-produce deceptive content by mimicking credible figures.
options.B: The avatars are a new technology that helps factories improve worker safety.
options.C: The avatars are being used to teach people how to identify fake medical advice.
options.D: The avatars are being sold to large companies to improve customer service.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中 Alex Ruani 使用此詞彙來描述 AI 虛擬人像利用其看似專業的外表（像真實醫生），大規模地欺騙觀眾以獲取信任。這是一種系統性、大規模的欺詐行為。選項 B 錯誤解讀了「industrialised」在此處指「大規模生產」而非工廠；選項 C 與文章警告大眾防範假建議的立場完全相反；選項 D 則完全偏離了醫療誤導的主題。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding AI-generated medical content?

options.A: AI technology is a helpful tool that doctors should adopt for patient education.
options.B: Social media platforms have successfully removed all fake AI-generated medical advice.
options.C: The public should be skeptical of AI-generated health advice and prioritize professional medical consultation.
options.D: The main danger of AI avatars is that they are too expensive for the average user to produce.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章的核心主旨在於警告大眾，社群媒體上充斥著由 AI 生成的虛假醫療建議，這些內容具有誤導性且可能危害健康。文章最後一段明確呼籲大眾應保持謹慎，並諮詢真正的專業醫師。選項 A 與文章警告的立場衝突；選項 B 與第六段提到「難以控制」的內容不符；選項 D 並非文章討論的重點，文中並未提及製作成本。
